question.problem:
A wildlife reserve is monitoring the population of a newly introduced species of deer. The habitat can sustain a maximum population of $850$ deer, but the herd is still below this limit. Since biologists began tracking the growth, the population reached $490$ deer on month $4$ and $600$ deer on month $12.$ On what month will the population reach $800$ deer? Round your answer to the nearest integer.

*Hint: You may assume that the population of deer, $P(t),$ increases at a rate that obeys an inhibited growth model, where $t$ is the time, in months.*
question.worked_solution:
The rate at which the population $P(t)$ changes is proportional to the difference between the maximum population and its current population. Therefore, we have the inhibited growth equation

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=k(a-P),
$$

where $a$ is the maximum production of the farm, and $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality.

In our case, $a=850$ deer, and we have

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=k(850-P).
$$

First, we integrate our differential equation by separating the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dP}{850-P} & =k\,dt \\ \int \frac{dP}{850-P} & =\int k\,\text{d}t \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡|850-P| & =kt+C\end{aligned}
$$

Since this is the solution to an inhibited growth equation, we have $850-P>0$ for all $t\ge 0.$ Next, we solve for $P(t),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}850-P & ={e}^{-kt-C} \\ 850-P & ={e}^{-C}{e}^{-kt} \\ 850-P & =K{e}^{-kt} \\ P & =850-K{e}^{-kt}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $K={e}^{-C}$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that, on month $4,$ the population reached $490$ deer. So, applying the condition $P(4)=490,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(4) & =490 \\ 850-K{e}^{-4k} & =490 \\ K{e}^{-4k} & =360.\end{aligned}
$$

We're also told that, on month $12,$ the population was $600$ deer. So, applying the condition $P(12)=600,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(12) & =600 \\ 850-K{e}^{-12k} & =600 \\ K{e}^{-12k} & =250.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, by dividing the result of the first condition by the result of the second, we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{K{e}^{-4k}}{K{e}^{-12k}} & =\frac{360}{250} \\ {e}^{8k} & =\frac{36}{25} \\ 8k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{36}{25}) \\ k & =\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{36}{25})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting back into the result of the first condition, we solve for $K:$

$$
\begin{aligned}K{e}^{-4\cdot (1/8)\operatorname{ln}⁡(36/25)} & =360 \\ K & =360{e}^{(1/2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(36/25)} \\ K & =360\sqrt{\frac{36}{25}} \\ K & =360\cdot \frac{6}{5} \\ K & =432\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following expression for $P(t):$

$$
P(t)=850-432{e}^{-(t/8)\operatorname{ln}⁡(36/25)}
$$

Finally, let $m$ be the month when the population reaches $800$ deer. Then, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(m) & =800 \\ 850-432{e}^{-km} & =800 \\ 50 & =432{e}^{-km} \\ {e}^{-km} & =\frac{50}{432} \\ -km & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{25}{216}) \\ m & =-\frac{1}{k}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{25}{216}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting in our value for $k,$ we conclude that the population will be $500$ deer on month

$$
m=\frac{-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{25}{216})}{\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{36}{25})}=47.309…≈47,
$$

rounded to the nearest month.
